topStories.headline: Shooting at Haight and Ashbury Leaves One Hospitalized; Investigation Ongoing
topStories.dek: Gunfire erupted at San Francisco's most famous intersection late Tuesday night, sending one person to the hospital and leaving spent shell casings and property damage behind.
topStories.body:
Gunfire broke out near Haight and Ashbury streets just after 11 p.m. on Tuesday, September 30, sending at least one person to the hospital and rattling the neighborhood around the city's most iconic intersection. San Francisco police responded within minutes after dispatch received the first calls at approximately 11:09 p.m., but officers found no injured victims at the intersection itself — only multiple spent shell casings and property damaged by gunfire.

Police dispatch records show that calls reporting shots fired came in from three nearby intersections within about a minute of each other: Haight and Ashbury streets, Haight and Masonic Avenue, and Fulton and Lyon streets. Whether those reports were connected — or whether residents heard the same shots from different vantage points — remained unclear as of press time. Shortly after the gunfire, a person with a gunshot wound arrived separately at an area hospital. SFPD has not confirmed whether that patient is connected to the Haight and Ashbury incident.

No arrests have been made and no suspect information has been released. The shooting remains under active investigation by SFPD. Anyone with information is asked to contact the department's tip line at 415-575-4444 or text 'SFPD' followed by a tip to TIP411.

SFist noted that gun violence is not common in the Haight-Ashbury area, and Hoodline reported that citywide gun-violence incidents in 2026 have been running 18 percent below the same period in 2025. San Francisco also logged its lowest annual homicide count since 1954 in 2025. Still, the incident at one of the neighborhood's busiest corners drew immediate concern from residents and business owners along the corridor.

topStories.headline: Construction Set to Begin Oct. 19 on Long-Stalled 203-Unit Divisadero Building — and Neighbors Are Not Happy About Who's Building It
topStories.dek: Greystar, the nation's largest corporate landlord, is poised to break ground on an eight-story apartment building at 400 Divisadero on October 19, reigniting a years-long debate about affordable housing and development on the corridor.
topStories.body:
After nearly a decade of delays, the vacant former Touchless Car Wash site at 400 Divisadero Street is finally headed for construction — but the project's new developer is drawing sharp criticism from neighborhood advocates. Public Works permits list an October 19 construction start date for the eight-story, 203-unit apartment building, with sidewalk and lane closures along Divisadero and Oak streets expected to accompany the groundbreaking.

Greystar, the South Carolina-based real estate giant that manages more than one million rental units nationally, stepped in this summer to take over the project from 4Terra Investments, which had completed much of the design and permitting work. Of the 203 planned units — 121 one-bedrooms and 82 two-bedrooms — only 20 are designated as permanently affordable housing. The project also includes roughly 1,850 square feet of ground-floor retail and 24 parking spaces.

The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council called Greystar 'the nation's largest corporate landlord and property manager' in a September post on its website, citing the company's history of federal antitrust investigations and tenant disputes in other markets. HANC noted that a prior plan had explored having the nonprofit Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation acquire the site for fully subsidized housing. D5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who championed the SHADE Act allowing the project to use older building codes and thus reduce construction costs, announced the Greystar deal and has backed it as the path most likely to actually deliver new housing on a site that had sat vacant for years.

BDE Architecture designed the podium-style building, which will feature a facade of stone veneer, stucco, and wood-look siding with bay windows, balconies, and blue accents. Construction is expected to cost approximately $85 million.

topStories.headline: HANC Invites Neighborhood to Hear Case Against Lurie's Rezoning Plan at October 9 Meeting
topStories.dek: The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council will host a public forum Thursday on what it calls 'fatal flaws' in Mayor Lurie's citywide upzoning proposal, which has already cleared the Planning Commission on a narrow 4–3 vote.
topStories.body:
The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council is hosting its October General Membership meeting on Thursday, October 9 at 7 p.m. at the Park Branch Library, 1833 Page St., with a focused discussion on Mayor Daniel Lurie's sweeping rezoning proposal and what HANC describes as its impact on Haight-Ashbury's rent-controlled housing stock and neighborhood-serving businesses.

Quintin Mecke, Executive Director of the Council of Community Housing Organizations (CCHO) — whose 16 member groups have built or rehabilitated roughly 30,000 permanently affordable housing units in San Francisco — will present the case that the proposal fails to address the city's affordable housing needs for most residents. HANC's own written critique identifies five areas of concern, including the risk of displacement of thousands of current tenants, insufficient protections for legacy retail businesses, and the failure to link new density along transit corridors with funding for expanded transit service.

The proposal passed the San Francisco Planning Commission on September 11 on a 4–3 vote, with all three supervisor-appointed commissioners in dissent, and now moves to the Board of Supervisors. A Land Use Committee hearing on the upzoning is tentatively scheduled for October 20 at City Hall, Room 250. HANC's October 15 meeting of its Commission Streamlining Task Force at City Hall, Room 408 is also on the calendar.

The Park Branch Library is located at 1833 Page St. in Haight-Ashbury. The meeting is free and open to all HANC members and the public.

events.title: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass 2026
events.location: Golden Gate Park (Hellman Hollow and multiple stages)
events.description: The beloved free festival returns to Golden Gate Park for three days of music across six stages, featuring Gillian Welch & David Rawlings, My Morning Jacket, Alison Krauss & Union Station, Old Crow Medicine Show, and dozens more. Admission is free; food and beverage vendors on site.

events.title: Lower Haight Community Cleanup
events.location: Tarragon Cafe, 200 Fillmore St, Lower Haight
events.description: Neighbors gather to clean up Lower Haight streets, with coffee and breakfast provided at the Tarragon Cafe starting point. Brought to you by local volunteers.

events.title: Prince vs. Michael at Madrone Art Bar
events.location: Madrone Art Bar, 500 Divisadero St, Lower Haight
events.description: The legendary monthly dance-off pits Prince against Michael Jackson as DJs spin album cuts, remixes, and rarities from both catalogs. 21+.

events.title: HANC General Meeting: 'Fatal Flaws in Lurie's Rezoning Proposal'
events.location: Park Branch Library, 1833 Page St, Haight-Ashbury
events.description: The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council hosts its monthly general meeting, featuring CCHO Executive Director Quintin Mecke on the impacts of Mayor Lurie's citywide upzoning plan on affordable housing and neighborhood retail. Open to the public.

events.title: SF's 1st Children's Business Fair
events.location: San Francisco County Fair Building, 1199 9th Ave, Golden Gate Park
events.description: San Francisco's inaugural Children's Business Fair brings roughly 40 kid entrepreneurs ages 5–14 to Golden Gate Park, selling handmade crafts, upcycled creations, and more. Free admission for visitors.

moreNews.headline: Pasta Supply Co. Eyes October Opening at 919 Cole St. in Cole Valley
moreNews.body: Chef Anthony Strong is aiming to open the third location of his popular pasta shop and restaurant at 919 Cole Street — the former Peet's Coffee that closed earlier this year — sometime this October. The 700-square-foot counter-service space will offer about 30 varieties of fresh pasta alongside sauces and pantry staples, with roughly 24 dine-in seats and daily lunch and dinner service. Strong, who has lived in Cole Valley for 12 years, crowdfunded the opening directly through the restaurant, with rewards including pasta subscriptions. Pasta Supply Co. first opened on Clement Street in 2023 and added a Mission location in 2024.

restaurants.name: Cha Cha Cha
restaurants.description: Haight Street institution since 1984 serving Caribbean tapas, paella, jerk chicken, and pitchers of house sangria in a lively, colorful dining room.

restaurants.name: Parada 22
restaurants.description: Veteran-owned neighborhood spot serving home-cooked Puerto Rican comfort food — mofongo, pernil asado, tostones, and rice and beans — daily from 10am.

restaurants.name: Magnolia Brewing – Haight
restaurants.description: Haight Street's landmark craft brewery and gastropub, reopened in late 2024 under new local ownership with a refreshed taproom, house-brewed beers, and elevated pub food.

restaurants.name: The Alembic
restaurants.description: Inventive American cocktail bar and restaurant on Haight Street with 100-plus bourbons and scotches, farm-driven small plates, and a cozy, dimly lit interior.

restaurants.name: Pork Store Cafe
restaurants.description: Much-loved Haight Street diner serving enormous portions of scratch-made breakfast and brunch at affordable prices since 1989.

restaurants.name: Escape From New York Pizza
restaurants.type: New York-style pizza by the slice
restaurants.description: San Francisco Legacy Business since 1986, slinging hot New York-style slices with creative toppings late into the night on Haight Street.

restaurants.name: Zam Zam
restaurants.description: One of the Haight's most storied dive bars, with Persian-themed décor, a circular bar, and perfectly made martinis in a setting unchanged for decades.

restaurants.name: Zazie
restaurants.description: Beloved Cole Valley French bistro open since 1992, famous for its weekend brunch with Provençal-inspired eggs, crêpes, and a sunny back patio.

restaurants.name: Beit Rima
restaurants.description: Award-winning Cole Valley spot serving Arabic comfort food — hand-kneaded bread, crispy falafel, chicken skewers, and za'atar-dusted pita — with a devoted neighborhood following.

restaurants.name: Cole Valley Tavern
restaurants.description: Neighborhood go-to American bar with a warm dining room, rotating food specials, and an ice cream window that draws lines on warm evenings.

restaurants.name: InoVino
restaurants.description: Intimate Cole Valley wine bar with an excellent selection of Italian bottles, solid pastas, and charcuterie-and-cheese boards in a cozy setting.

restaurants.name: Crepes On Cole
restaurants.description: Casual Cole Valley standby open late most nights, offering sweet and savory crêpes, burgers, and beer in a relaxed neighbourhood setting.

restaurants.name: Toronado
restaurants.description: Lower Haight craft-beer pilgrimage site with 50 taps of rare and sought-after brews, sticker-plastered walls, and a cash-only, no-nonsense vibe — now under new local ownership as of June 2026.

restaurants.name: Bar Jabroni
restaurants.description: Lively Lower Haight wine bar pouring chilled reds and orange wines alongside small plates like beef tartare with Szechuan peppercorns and house-made focaccia.

restaurants.name: Nopalito
restaurants.description: Organic, from-scratch Mexican cooking from the Nopa team, plating blue-corn tacos, carnitas, and mole made with local and sustainable ingredients.

restaurants.name: Noc Noc
restaurants.description: Lower Haight bar with trippy, Tim Burton-esque décor that is a neighbourhood fixture — only in San Francisco.

restaurants.name: Danny Coyle's
restaurants.description: Friendly Lower Haight Irish bar open until 2am, with a great tap selection, sports on TV, and a loyal neighbourhood crowd.

restaurants.name: Woods Lowside
restaurants.description: Casual Lower Haight bar with crisp, dry house beers, natural wines, Detroit-style pizza from Joyride Pizza on site, and a heated back patio.

restaurants.name: Bambino's Ristorante
restaurants.description: Charming old-school Italian restaurant in Cole Valley with hearty classic pastas and a warm, neighbourhood trattoria feel.

restaurants.name: Double Black
restaurants.description: New Cole Valley coffee shop inside the Yardsale outdoor apparel store, drawing queues for iced hojicha lattes with black-sesame cold foam.

hotels.name: Stanyan Park Hotel
hotels.description: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, this 1904 Beaux Arts Victorian hotel sits across from Golden Gate Park and includes a daily continental breakfast and weekday wine-and-cheese reception.

hotels.name: The Metro Hotel
hotels.description: Family-owned 23-room boutique hotel on Divisadero with original artwork throughout, a private garden, and a welcoming eco-conscious ethos steps from Haight-Ashbury.

shops.name: Booksmith
shops.description: Haight Street's landmark independent bookstore since 1976, offering a wide selection of new titles and hosting more than 200 author events per year.

shops.name: Amoeba Music
shops.description: Enormous independent music store claiming the world's largest selection of new and used vinyl, CDs, DVDs, and posters — a pilgrimage site for music fans since 1990.

shops.name: Love on Haight
shops.description: SF Legacy Business since 1989 selling vibrant tie-dye clothing and accessories by more than 175 local and international artists, keeping the Haight's countercultural spirit alive.

shops.name: Wasteland
shops.description: Glamorous Haight Street vintage and resale boutique with a carefully curated mix of high-end secondhand fashion and designer pieces — buy, sell, or trade.

shops.name: Piedmont Boutique
shops.description: An unofficial Haight landmark identifiable by the giant fishnet-stocking legs hanging from the second-floor window, selling costumes, festival wear, and dramatic accessories.

shops.name: Relic Vintage
shops.description: Go-to Haight Street vintage shop since 2012, housing carefully selected garments from the 1920s through the 1980s and a strong collection of statement accessories.

shops.name: Say Cheese
shops.description: Cole Valley institution since 1976 offering an extensive world cheese selection alongside charcuterie, wines, olives, artisanal snacks, and loaded deli sandwiches.

shops.name: San Francisco Mercantile
shops.description: Haight Street retail shop partnered with San Francisco Heritage, selling locally made gifts, detailed neighborhood maps, art, and keepsakes by Bay Area artists.

shops.name: Woot Bear
shops.type: Designer toy store and art gallery
shops.description: Haight Street collectible toy boutique and gallery hosting monthly art shows alongside a floor-to-ceiling selection of designer figures from Tokidoki, Pop Mart, Kidrobot, and more.

shops.name: Pipe Dreams
shops.description: SF Legacy Business at 1376 Haight Street and a touchstone of the neighbourhood's countercultural roots since the 1960s.

shops.name: Cole Hardware
shops.type: Independent hardware and home goods store
shops.description: Beloved Cole Valley institution and local alternative to big-box hardware stores, stocking household essentials, plants, and an eclectic range of gifts.

artEntertainment.name: The DeLuxe
artEntertainment.description: Beloved Haight Street jazz venue reborn in June 2026 after a three-year closure: restored Art Deco interior, rebuilt stage, upgraded sound, craft cocktails, and live music seven nights a week.

artEntertainment.name: Haight Street Art Center
artEntertainment.type: Non-profit poster art gallery and printmaking studio
artEntertainment.description: Non-profit gallery and printmaking studio in Lower Haight dedicated to the history and culture of poster art, with free rotating exhibitions open Thursday through Sunday noon–6pm.

artEntertainment.name: Woot Bear Gallery
artEntertainment.type: Designer toy and contemporary art gallery
artEntertainment.description: Monthly rotating art exhibitions alongside a curated selection of collectible designer toys, featuring artists from around the world in a compact Haight Street space.

artEntertainment.name: Amoeba Music (Live Events)
artEntertainment.type: In-store live music and events venue
artEntertainment.description: The Haight Street record store regularly hosts free in-store performances and release events across genres, making it a casual live-music destination in its own right.

artEntertainment.name: Kezar Stadium
artEntertainment.description: Century-old stadium in the southeast corner of Golden Gate Park, the original home of the San Francisco 49ers, now hosting amateur sports leagues, track workouts, high school events, and FC City matches.

gymsRecreation.name: HAUM Studios – Haight-Ashbury
gymsRecreation.description: Award-winning, LGBTQ+-owned yoga studio at Stanyan Street offering Vinyasa, Hatha, Slow Flow, Restorative Yoga, soundbaths, and breathwork classes for all levels, seven days a week.

gymsRecreation.name: Folk Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: Community-centred yoga and fitness studio on Divisadero offering a wide range of class styles including Flow, Restore, and prenatal yoga with highly rated instructors.

gymsRecreation.name: Kezar Pavilion
gymsRecreation.description: 1924 indoor arena adjacent to Kezar Stadium managed by SF Recreation and Parks, hosting basketball, volleyball, roller derby, and the Pro-Am Summer Basketball League.

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park Panhandle
gymsRecreation.description: The slim, tree-lined Panhandle strip extending east from Golden Gate Park is a beloved daily running, cycling, and dog-walking green space anchoring the neighbourhood.

gymsRecreation.name: Buena Vista Park
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's oldest public park, offering wooded trails, sweeping city views, and a popular off-leash dog area on a forested hill above Haight-Ashbury.
gymsRecreation.address: Buena Vista Ave W & Haight St
